en.title: Longest Peak Obtainable by Rearranging
en.description:
Choose any numbers from the array and rearrange them into a sequence that strictly increases and then strictly decreases. The two parts share the peak, and either part may consist of just the peak, so purely increasing, purely decreasing, and single-element sequences are also valid. Return the maximum length.

This site uses a standard input/output protocol; ranges not given by the source are stated explicitly.
en.input: The first line contains N, and the second line contains N integers. The source gives no numeric range; this site uses 1≤N≤200000 and elements in −10⁹..10⁹.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: Example 1: 1, 2 is already a peak, of length 2. Example 2: you can arrange 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 2, of length 6. Example 3: strictness forbids repeating the peak value, so only one 5 can be used.
hints: The maximum value can be used only once, at the peak, and every other value can appear at most once on each side. So the answer is 1 plus the sum of min(frequency,2) over the non-maximum values.
